title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 1 at Steelers Post Game Press Conference | Atlanta Falcons
headline: Bijan Robinson ran for 173 yards and Stefanski says Atlanta will keep leaning on him, while Cooper Rush started on two days' prep with Penix and Tua still without an update.
summary: Stefanski blamed the Week 1 road loss to Pittsburgh on penalties (nine, mostly post-snap), turnovers including a defensive score for the Steelers, and a kickoff return touchdown. He praised the team's effort but said they weren't sharp enough. Cooper Rush had only two days to prepare, and Stefanski said plenty of the original game plan carried over. He had no update on when Penix or Tua might return. Bijan Robinson ran for 173 yards, and Stefanski said Atlanta will keep leaning on him while also finding ways to get other players touches. Kyle Pitts had no catches, which Stefanski put down to holding penalties, batted balls and Pittsburgh's defense. On defense, Stefanski liked the third-down result (3-of-13) against a quick-release quarterback, and Za'Darius Smith, Bralen Trice and Yasir Abdullah all got reps while roles for the new guys are still being sorted out. He declined to look ahead to the lineup question or the next game beyond saying it is a home game against a division opponent. A player who left the game early needs tests, and the injury's severity is unknown.

injuries.detail: Stefanski had no update on when he or Tua might be back.
No update on his return, per Stefanski.
Stefanski said a player was 'close to 100' after a question about health, and it was probably Rush. Rush was healthy enough to start.

signals.claim: Robinson will remain the focal point of the offense and keep getting heavy touches in upcoming games.
signals.note: A 173-yard game plus a stated commitment to lean on him keeps him a workhorse RB1, though Stefanski also wants to spread touches around.
signals.quote: We're going to keep leaning on him

signals.claim: Rush was healthy enough to start and will stay in the quarterback role while Penix and Tua are out.
signals.note: Rush is the starter by default with Penix and Tua without an update, and the turnovers and pressure hurt the passing game.
signals.quote: Cooper was healthy and you know, could start.

signals.note: His return timeline is unknown, which leaves the QB spot uncertain for QB-dependent fantasy assets.
signals.quote: I don't have an update.

signals.note: No timeline for his return, so Atlanta's QB situation is murky.
signals.quote: I don't have an update.

signals.claim: Pitts should see more pass-game opportunities once penalties and batted balls stop costing them.
signals.note: He was held without a catch and the coach gave no specific plan to get him more targets, so he is a wait-and-see TE.
signals.quote: those are opportunities that you're not getting in the pass game

signals.claim: Smith will keep a meaningful rotational pass-rush role.
signals.note: He logged a lot of reps and a sack, which is relevant for IDP leagues.
signals.quote: we got a lot of reps from Za'darius

signals.note: He played in a defensive line rotation whose roles are still being worked out.
signals.quote: a lot of new guys that are we're figuring out the roles for them

signals.note: He was recently acquired and his role is still being defined, so IDP value is unclear.

signals.claim: Strand was not going to play in Week 1 with Rush healthy.
signals.note: He is the backup QB and was never considered for action, so he only matters if Rush is hurt.
signals.quote: I'm very proud of his development.

topics.detail: Atlanta had nine penalties, mostly post-snap holds from getting beaten quickly. A kickoff return touchdown and a defensive score for Pittsburgh were the key swing plays.
Stefanski said the pass rush problems were not only the offensive line's fault. Receivers, chips and timing are all involved, and he called Pittsburgh's rushers excellent.
After kicker Nick missed kicks, Stefanski said he doesn't expect him to be perfect and expects him to respond.
Atlanta held Pittsburgh to roughly 3-of-13 on third down and limited them to a short-field touchdown. Stefanski credited the rush and coverage working together against a quick-release quarterback.
A player left the game early and has tests pending, so the severity is unknown. The player was not clearly named in the transcript.
Atlanta plays at home next week against a division opponent, whom Stefanski did not name. He wants to move on quickly.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps His First Regular-Season Win as Head Coach
headline: Derrick Henry scored three TDs in the 41-23 win, but Baltimore's WR room is thin after an in-game injury (apparently Ja'Kobi Lane, hand) and Chris Moore stepped up with a career day.
summary: Minter was proud of the team after the opener, a 41-23 win over the Colts. He praised the offense, which started fast under first-time play caller Declan Doyle, and singled out Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, the offensive line and Zay Flowers. The defense struggled on the first drive, then settled in and created turnovers. Roquan Smith's interception flipped momentum and set up a short field, and Marlon Humphrey forced a turnover. Minter called Henry's performance a tribute to his preparation and work habits. The offense closed the game with a six-minute running drive, and the line took over. The team was shorthanded at wide receiver after an in-game injury. Minter said there were no real updates on the hand injury and the staff will see how it looks this week. He credited Chris Moore, who was activated for the game, with a career-high 174 all-purpose yards, and pointed to depth in the WR room. He also voiced steady confidence in the kicker (the transcript says "Tyler loop"), who made his kicks after a shaky preseason.

injuries.detail: A reporter said he appeared to have a cast on his hand after leaving the game. Minter gave no real update and said the team will see how it looks. The name was garbled in the transcript ("Jacoby"), so the match is a best guess.

signals.claim: Henry remains the featured back and the closer in the run game, including with the team shorthanded at WR.
signals.note: He scored three TDs and carried the late six-minute drive, which supports his workload and TD upside.
signals.quote: that's who Derrick is.

signals.claim: Moore, activated for the opener, produced 174 all-purpose yards and may keep a bigger role while the WR room is thin.
signals.note: If a WR is out, Moore could see more targets or returns, though he is a deep-league or watch-list option for now.
signals.quote: he had a career high. I think he had 174 all purpose yards.

signals.claim: His availability for next week is uncertain pending evaluation of a hand injury.
signals.note: A hand injury could open WR snaps for others, so monitor his practice status before lineup lock.
signals.quote: no real updates right now. We'll kind of see what it looks like.

signals.claim: The offense under Declan Doyle looked sharp from the first drive, with Jackson running the operation.
signals.note: A strong opener under the new play caller supports confidence in the Baltimore offense.
signals.quote: Lamar just running the operation.

signals.claim: Flowers was named among the offensive standouts, and the WR room is shorthanded.
signals.note: He is the top WR with a possible injury elsewhere in the room, so his target share is worth watching.

topics.detail: The offense came out fast in Declan Doyle's first game as play caller. Minter credited the preparation over the extra time before the opener, and said the offensive line took over late.
The defense was shaky on the first drive, then settled in. Roquan Smith's interception and Marlon Humphrey's forced turnover set the tone, and the defense got the fourth-down call it wanted.
Minter said his confidence in the kicker never wavered after a preseason with a few misses, and he was glad to see him make his kicks.
Minter stressed that the 70-man roster is ready to play when called on. The staff will decide this week what is needed to get the WR room ready for next week.

title: Joe Brady Talks His First Victory As An NFL Head Coach
headline: DJ Moore debuted with a big game and Dalton Kincaid looked healthy and dynamic. Brady says Moore 'opens it up for everybody' and that Kincaid is a matchup issue. Josh Palmer made the game-winning connection. The run game was lacking, and Detroit comes on a four-day turnaround.
summary: Joe Brady was proud of his first head coaching win, a 36-31 victory at Houston. He said it was not clean in any phase, and the offense started slowly and had a critical three-and-out. The team wishes it had run the ball better. He praised Josh Allen's play, the O-line's pass protection against a dominant pass rush, and a defense that forced two takeaways and made the closing stop. DJ Moore got high praise for his debut, with Brady crediting him with stretching the field and making the whole offense better. Brady also singled out Dalton Kincaid as a matchup problem who is stronger in the run game and a better offense when on the field. He explained that he was aggressive on the late shot to Josh Palmer, and that he wants Allen to trust the play call and take what is open. On defense, he said Gregory Rousseau is embracing a new position in a two-point stance and should get more comfortable. The team has a short week and needs to clean up mistakes before Detroit.

injuries.detail: Has struggled to stay healthy. Brady said he looked strong and is only going to allow them to get him on the field a little more, and wants to get his body ready for the short week.

signals.claim: Moore will be a featured big-play and downfield target who opens up the offense, with an established connection with Josh Allen.
signals.note: Moore had a big debut and a touchdown, and Brady called him big for the offense, which suggests a strong target share.
signals.quote: He opens it up for everybody right.

signals.claim: Kincaid will see an expanded role in multiple personnel groupings, including more big-personnel looks, as a matchup problem.
signals.note: Brady said the team is better with him on the field and is trying to get him more snaps, though health remains a concern on a short week.
signals.quote: he's a matchup issue

signals.claim: Palmer will continue to be a trusted option for Allen in key situations after the game-winning post.
signals.note: Brady praised him for making the most of his coverages, but the target volume is uncertain since Allen is spreading the ball around.
signals.quote: Josh Palmer just doing his job

signals.claim: The offense will keep taking shots downfield and Allen will take what is open without worrying about who is in the position.
signals.note: Brady's endorsement of aggressive play-calling, plus a good pass-protection plan, supports Allen's passing production.
signals.quote: just trust the play call

signals.claim: The run game needs to be better after underperforming, but Moore's presence should open lanes for Cook.
signals.note: Brady admitted the run game struggled, which could limit Cook's production in the short term, but it should improve.

signals.claim: Rousseau is playing a new position in a two-point stance and will get more comfortable as the season goes on.
signals.note: Alongside Chubb and Oliver, the scheme fits his skills, which is a good sign for IDP managers.
signals.quote: I think the scheme fits fits Greg

topics.detail: Buffalo plays Detroit in four days. Brady said mistakes across offense, defense and special teams must be cleaned up quickly.
The O-line, backs, tight ends and receivers all contributed to protecting Allen against a strong pass rush. The only major issue was an early sack.
The defense had two takeaways and made a closing stop in the two-minute situation after giving up a big conversion inside the ten.
Brady said he likes aggressive late-game decisions and wants to have the ball in his hands in critical moments.

title: Dave Canales on Week 1 game vs. Bears
headline: Panthers lost 59-37 to the Bears; Canales liked Bryce Young's rhythm and deep shots to Jalen Coker, but Bobby Brown's injury is unresolved and the run game and TMac matchups fell short.
summary: Canales was clearly disappointed after the Panthers allowed 59 points and 550 yards, the most in team history, in the Week 1 loss to Chicago. He pinned the defensive failures on execution and fundamentals, not scheme or surprises, and said he would not make declarations until he watches film. He said penalties extended Bears drives and that 17 points off turnovers does not explain 59. He was positive about offensive coordinator Brad's first game calling plays, citing good rhythm, concepts the team is comfortable with, and a few explosive plays. He still said the offense missed chances, settling for field goals and failing to win a one-on-one with Tetairoa McMillan on a failed fourth down. He praised Bryce Young for extending plays, using his legs, and hitting nice deep balls to Jalen Coker, and he called the interception before the half an aggressive play. On the defensive line, he said effort was fine but players got out of their gaps on run plays. He addressed Derrick Brown's offsides and roughing-the-passer penalties, and said Bobby Brown was working through something but came back to finish the game, with more information to come.

injuries.detail: Went down a couple of times and appeared to be in pain, but returned and finished the game. Canales said he is working through some things and the team will share more information later.

signals.claim: Young will keep running the offense with the same rhythm and willingness to extend plays and make throws downfield.
signals.note: Canales praised Young's play, mobility and deep accuracy, which supports his fantasy outlook as a rhythm passer who adds rushing value.
signals.quote: I really loved the way he played

signals.claim: Coker will remain a primary target on downfield shots from Young.
signals.note: Canales singled out Young's nice balls down the field to Coker, a sign of his deep-target role.
signals.quote: hit some nice balls down the field to Jalen

signals.claim: McMillan is expected to win one-on-one matchups in key situations after losing on the failed fourth down.
signals.note: The staff trusts McMillan in contested one-on-one spots, so he should keep getting those targets, but he didn't convert here.
signals.quote: We had one on one with Tmac. You know, we expect those guys to win

signals.claim: More information on Brown's physical condition will be provided after the team evaluates him.
signals.note: His status is unclear, so monitor practice reports; it matters mainly for the defensive line and run defense.
signals.quote: He's just working through some stuff.

signals.claim: Brown is frustrated by his offsides and roughing-the-passer penalties and is expected to clean up his discipline.
signals.note: His penalties extended Bears drives; the quote is from a defender-focused answer, so the fantasy impact is IDP-only.
signals.quote: he's sick about the offsides.

topics.detail: Canales blamed execution and players leaving their responsibilities in the run game, not a scheme issue. He said the team backed the coordinator but will watch film before assigning responsibility.
He was pleased with Brad's first game calling plays, praising the timely calls and cohesion. He wanted more downs and a better run game, though he said the offense found the run game later.

Penalties were about even, but their timing extended Bears drives. The Panthers had a fumble, an interception before the half, a punt fumble and a personal foul at midfield that gave the Bears short fields.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' performance vs. Panthers in season opener | Press Conference
headline: Bears' run game dominated in the 59-37 opener: Swift and Monangai both produced, Caleb Williams started hot, and Rome Odunze and Cole Kmet were highlighted.
summary: Ben Johnson said the Bears came out of the heat in Charlotte relatively healthy and credited camp conditioning work. He pointed to takeaways, including a muffed punt and a punch-out, as momentum swings. He said he didn't think he called a good first half, but the players made plays anyway. In his view the story of the game was the rushing attack, with credit going to the offensive line, tight ends and blocking receivers. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both did a great job, and Caleb Williams added value with his legs. Johnson praised Williams for getting quickly to checkdowns, for his preparation, and for the touchdown throw to Cole Kmet. He also singled out Rome Odunze's sideline catch and praised a receiver who scored a late touchdown after a very consistent week of practice. The coach defended the aggressive fourth-and-two from his own 21 without committing to repeating it, and he stressed continued improvement in all three phases.

signals.claim: Williams is processing well, getting the ball out quickly to checkdowns, and adds value as a runner.
signals.note: The coach's strong endorsement of his process and rushing contributions supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: he came out hot.

signals.claim: Swift remains a key part of a run game that controlled the opener.
signals.note: He just received an extension and the coach highlighted the rushing success, which points to continued heavy usage.
signals.quote: he earned it. Every step of it.

signals.claim: Monangai is a productive part of the backfield and had the long run that broke free.
signals.note: He is sharing a productive rushing workload alongside Swift and showed big-play ability.
signals.quote: I don't know the long one there uh was that Kyle that broke free.

signals.claim: Odunze is a reliable sideline target who makes contested catches.
signals.note: The coach singled out his sideline catch as who he is, which signals trust as a primary receiver.
signals.quote: You see a guy like Rome go up and make that catch on the sideline.

signals.claim: Kmet caught a well-thrown touchdown in the end zone from Williams and was part of the run-blocking effort.
signals.note: A red-zone touchdown from Williams is a good sign for his scoring role.
signals.quote: Cole made a heck of a catch there too.

topics.detail: Johnson went for it on fourth and two from his own 21, felt good about it, and said repeating it depends on the game and situation.
A muffed punt, a punch-out and a late interception produced momentum, and the Bears scored a touchdown and forced a turnover at the end of the first half to take a seven-point lead into the break.
Johnson said the offensive line, tight ends and receivers all blocked well, and the rushing attack was the story of the game.
Johnson wants improvement in all three phases each week and expects dips along the way in a long season.

title: Zac Taylor: "Excited For The Win" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals beat Tampa Bay 33-27 behind four takeaways. Mike Gesicki is the offense's trusted two-minute and red-zone target, and Tee Higgins made the clinching catch.
summary: Zac Taylor called the 33-27 Week 1 win imperfect but a good one. He said the team had worked a long time on closing out games, and the offense did that in the final three-to-four-minute drill. The defense forced four turnovers that led to about 24 points, and the kicker (apparently Evan McPherson) hit four field goals. Taylor praised Mike Gesicki's chemistry and green-light freedom with Joe Burrow, especially in the two-minute drill and the red zone. He said Burrow managed the game well, with few incompletions and few second-and-longs, and that the offensive line handled Tampa's blitz package and opened run lanes. He said Tee Higgins' late third-down catch to clinch the game was as big as a catch gets, and that Burrow picked that play himself. Taylor wanted to get his top receivers involved but did not force the ball, which left a one-catch line for at least one top weapon, apparently Ja'Marr Chase. On defense he liked the young players' growth, the pass rush that dirtied the pocket, and hometown safety Bryan Cook's forced fumble and fumble recovery. He said a tough road game is next.

signals.claim: Gesicki will keep his green-light, ad-lib role with Burrow in two-minute and red-zone situations.
signals.note: Taylor trusts him as a go-to option in high-leverage situations, which supports his TE streaming and touchdown upside.
signals.quote: we give him that green light

signals.claim: Burrow will keep trusting Higgins on key third-down and game-clinching throws.
signals.note: Higgins was the chosen target on the clinching third-down slant, which shows his standing as Burrow's go-to option in key moments.
signals.quote: Joe trusts him.

signals.note: Taylor praised Burrow's rhythm and game management, and the offense scored 33 despite a pick-six.
signals.quote: So performance on Joe really good.

signals.claim: Taylor wants top receivers involved but won't force targets when the game script is working.
signals.note: Chase appears to have had a quiet line in a game that stayed balanced, so his volume depends on game flow.
signals.quote: we want to get them as involved as possible

signals.claim: Brown is trusted as a receiver against man coverage in late-game situations.
signals.note: He picked up a key first down as a receiver on the final drive, which suggests a role beyond rushing in the two-minute drill.
signals.quote: Chase Brown does a great job versus man coverage.

signals.note: Meyers (name garbled in the captions) caught the first pass of the final drive and was praised for his awareness. That could be a small usage bump, but it is one play.
signals.quote: Has the awareness to stay in bounds

signals.claim: Knight is gaining trust as a young defender and is playing faster.
signals.note: He finished the early touchdown play and Taylor singled him out, which is a good sign for defensive IDP value.
signals.quote: they're playing faster

signals.note: Cook, a Cincinnati native, had a forced fumble and a fumble recovery, which gives him IDP appeal.
signals.quote: Bryan Cook coming up with a forced fumble and a fumble recovery

topics.detail: The offense took an aggressive approach in the final drive, using short passes, a drawn offside penalty, a quarterback sneak and a kneel-down. Taylor said they had rehearsed it in camp, including against Chicago.
Four turnovers and constant pressure on Baker Mayfield changed the narrative about last year's defensive mistakes, according to Taylor. He said the defensive line gave the team an energy boost.
Taylor credited the line and the coaches for preparing for Tampa's difficult blitz package. He said the run game had good holes early.
Taylor called the crowd a weapon. It drew false starts, delay-of-game penalties and an early timeout from Tampa, which he said may have decided a one-score game.
Taylor said a really tough road game comes next and the team must get ready for it. He did not name the opponent.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Jaguars: September 13th, 2026
headline: Browns were blown out at Jacksonville; Monken defended Deshaun Watson without committing to him as the Week 3 starter, and Zion Johnson left briefly with an ankle issue before returning.
summary: Monken took blame for a poor road loss, citing delay-of-game and false-start penalties, a first-drive turnover, and an offense that went three-and-out, three-and-out and two-and-out, which kept the defense on the field. He said the loss was not all Deshaun Watson's fault and pointed to play-calling, protection and execution. He would not confirm Watson as the starter for next week in Tampa, saying he hadn't watched the tape and that everything would be evaluated. He said Watson was not playing tentatively and that the first interception was a ball he let rip. Monken praised the four rookie starters on offense (KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, Spencer Fano and Austin Barber) as future tremendous players, while acknowledging Concepcion's turnover. Zion Johnson was hurt early but came back in, and Monken said they would see how he feels the next day. He also explained that the starters stayed in late for in-game reps and confidence, and that the defense had to rotate because of the heat and the offense's quick drives.

injuries.detail: Went down looking bad, then returned to the game. Monken said the adrenaline may be masking it and they will see how he is tomorrow.

signals.claim: Watson's status as the starting QB for Week 3 at Tampa will be evaluated after tape review, not guaranteed.
signals.note: Monken declined to commit to Watson as the starter, so his job security is a risk for fantasy managers.

signals.claim: Monken does not think Watson played tentatively and spread the blame across the offense.
signals.note: Monken defended Watson's play, but the offense's poor rhythm makes his fantasy output uncertain.
signals.quote: He let that ball rip.

signals.claim: Concepcion, a rookie, started and is expected to be a tremendous player.
signals.note: He is a rookie starter at WR with the coach's confidence, despite his turnover.
signals.quote: Casey and Denzel are going to be tremendous players.

signals.claim: Boston started as a rookie and is expected to become a tremendous player.
signals.note: He is in the starting lineup with strong backing from the coach.
signals.quote: Casey and Denzel are going to be tremendous players.

signals.claim: Johnson's availability will be clearer after tomorrow's check-in.
signals.note: An injury to an offensive lineman could matter for an already struggling offense.
signals.quote: We'll have to see tomorrow when he gets back in.

signals.claim: Fano, a rookie lineman, started and is expected to become a tremendous player.
signals.note: He has the coach's confidence at tackle or guard, which is relevant to protection quality.
signals.quote: I think Spencer is going to be a tremendous player.

topics.detail: Delay-of-game and false-start penalties, along with slow huddle and substitution operations, hurt the offense. Monken took responsibility and said it needs to be cleaned up.

A first-drive turnover was followed by repeated three-and-outs against the top run defense, which limited the play-action and run game. A two-minute drive before halftime was derailed by holding and procedural penalties.
The defense was forced to rotate early because of the heat and the offense's short drives. Monken said the offense did not allow Jacksonville to be forced into a substitution pattern.
Monken kept the starters in late to get reps and confidence, and the last drive started with a run game that had been missing.

title: Campbell on Lions Week 1 performance
headline: Jahmyr Gibbs was the featured back with 24 carries before overtime and is in the best shape of his career. Campbell called him the 'hot hand' but said the staff will monitor his workload. An unnamed player's injury scan came back negative, though it may be hip-related.
summary: Campbell was happy with a Week 1 overtime win over the Saints, a game the Lions nearly gave away after leading 21-0. He credited the defense for three takeaways, a shutdown of the run game, and pressure on the quarterback, including on the final two-point try. He praised Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs for big performances, and said Aidan Hutchinson played really well and Derrick Barnes was all over the field. He also named Rock for a big play at the end and Tay Martin as a special teams difference-maker. The offense fizzled after the early lead, and the offensive line was up and down, though the team rushed for about 160 yards and was close to breaking several more runs open. Gibbs got a heavy workload, and Campbell said he is in the best shape he has been in with the team, but the staff will monitor him. Chris Olave found openings against the defense, and Campbell said the secondary needs to tighten up mentally and get to its spots quicker, though he was not concerned. Campbell mentioned a scan that came back negative on an unnamed player, but said it could still be something hip-related. The Lions play Buffalo next on a short week.

injuries.detail: Campbell said a scan came back negative, which is good news, but it may be more hip-related and the player is not yet out of the woods. The player was not named in the transcript.

signals.claim: Gibbs will remain the lead back with a heavy workload, though the staff will monitor his carries.
signals.note: He had 24 carries before overtime and Campbell called him the hot hand, which points to a high-volume role, with some risk that the team manages his touches.
signals.quote: that guy's our hot hand

signals.note: Campbell singled him out for a big-time Week 1 performance, which supports his target-leader status.
signals.quote: I thought Saint Brown, and Gibbs had some really big time performances for us.

signals.note: Campbell praised his play, and the defense pressured the Saints quarterback, which is good for his sack potential.
signals.quote: Hutch played really well.

signals.note: Campbell said Barnes was all over the field and you could feel it, which is a positive for IDP value.
signals.quote: Derrick Barnes was all over the field.

topics.detail: The Lions had three takeaways and shut down the run, which Campbell called their bread and butter. They also got pressure on the quarterback, including on the final two-point attempt. The secondary got strung out at times, and Campbell said the group needs to be quicker and cleaner mentally.

The offense stalled after taking an early lead and needs to be more efficient. The line blocked well in the run game, rushing for about 160 yards, but several runs were close to breaking open with just a little more blocking at the second level.
The Lions play Buffalo on a short week, and Campbell said they must clean up errors quickly. He noted that Buffalo is also on a short week.
Campbell said Tay Martin was a difference-maker on special teams.

At the end of regulation, Campbell considered going for it on fourth down but chose to let the clock run and trust the defense. He expected the Saints to go for two in overtime. He also said he thought the Lions had lost on a fumble ruling that went their way because the passer's arm was moving forward.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans vs Bills, Missed Opportunities | Full Q&A
headline: Ryans praised the David Montgomery/Woody Marks 'one-two punch' and a poised C.J. Stroud after a Week 1 loss to Buffalo; Henry To'oTo'o is being evaluated for a shoulder injury.
summary: Ryans credited Buffalo but pinned the loss on Houston's defense, which gave up too many explosive plays and missed chances to make plays on the ball. The Texans lost the turnover battle 2-0, and Buffalo scored off both giveaways. He was pleased with the offense, saying it drove the ball consistently and scored more than enough to win. He singled out the offensive line for controlling the line of scrimmage, especially in short-yardage situations. Montgomery and Woody Marks both ran well, and Ryans said he loves where the 'one-two punch' at running back is headed. He said C.J. Stroud was in control all game, made good decisions, and showed the confidence and growth he displayed in camp. He would not let the two lost fumbles overshadow that performance. Defensively, he said the D-line was neutralized early but improved in the second half, and the coverage must be tighter. He also admitted the team had no one watching Josh Allen on his scramble touchdown. Henry To'oTo'o left before the final drive and is being evaluated for a shoulder injury. Ryans brushed off a question about preparing for Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

injuries.detail: Left the game before the final drive; being evaluated for a shoulder injury, with more information expected over the next couple of days.

signals.claim: Montgomery will continue to share the lead RB role with Woody Marks in a two-back rotation.
signals.note: Montgomery had an effective Week 1 and remains a key part of a committee backfield behind a line that is winning in short yardage.
signals.quote: David did an outstanding job today

signals.claim: Marks will remain a significant part of the Texans' RB rotation alongside Montgomery.
signals.note: Ryans praised the 'one-two punch', which suggests Marks has a stable role in the committee.
signals.quote: Woody also ran it well.

signals.claim: Stroud is playing with confidence and command, and the two lost fumbles will not change the team's trust in him.
signals.note: The coach's strong endorsement of Stroud's decision-making and poise is a good sign for his fantasy outlook despite the turnovers.
signals.quote: CJ was very much in control the entire game.

topics.detail: Houston gave up too many explosive plays and missed chances to intercept passes. Ryans said Reed Blankenship, Kamari Lassiter and Calen Bullock each had a hand on a ball. The front was neutralized early but improved in the second half, and the secondary must be tighter.
Houston lost the turnover battle 2-0, with Buffalo scoring off both. Ryans called it the difference in the game.
Ryans said the line controlled the line of scrimmage, especially in short-yardage situations, and that helped the run game.
Ryans said the defense was not tied together from front to coverage on Allen's first-half touchdown scramble, because no one had eyes on the quarterback.

title: Liam Coen Recaps Dominant Victory Over Browns: "A True Team Win" | Press Conference
headline: Jacksonville's 34-10 Week 1 win was a spread-around offense: Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange all scored, Bhayshul Tuten ran well, and Trevor Lawrence started fast.
summary: Coen called the win over Cleveland a true team win built on a fast start, physical play and a defense that held the Browns to three points after a short field. He praised Parker Washington's diving touchdown and said he was glad to get him going early. He liked how Trevor Lawrence spread the ball around, played well off schedule and was well protected. Coen said Lawrence's fast start was planned: the staff practiced the opening script more on Friday, and Lawrence had a strong grasp of the plan. Coen said he wants Lawrence to lean on his mobility early in games. He singled out rookie Josh Cameron for a contested touchdown catch and a good comeback route. He also said he deliberately wanted Brenton Strange involved after Cameron's score, and Strange caught a touchdown on the next drive. Bhayshul Tuten got praise for yards after contact and trusting his reads, though Coen said the offense could have gotten to more outside zone. Coen's main cleanup item was kickoff coverage.

signals.claim: Washington remains a featured early-game target in the passing offense.
signals.note: He scored a diving touchdown on a well-run route against man coverage, and Coen wanted him involved early.
signals.quote: pleased with the way that we started fast, especially getting Parker going early.

signals.claim: The offense will keep scripting early plays and using Lawrence's mobility to avoid slow starts.
signals.note: A planned fast start, strong protection and off-schedule playmaking point to a stable QB1 outlook.
signals.quote: I was definitely pleased with the way that Trevor ran the offense today.

signals.claim: Cameron will keep getting targets as a contested-catch receiver after a touchdown in his first real NFL action.
signals.note: Coen said the quarterbacks trust him, which could make him a touchdown-dependent depth option.
signals.quote: the quarterbacks do trust him to put it in his vicinity

signals.claim: Coen will deliberately look to get Strange involved in the passing game.
signals.note: Coen called a play to get Strange the ball after Cameron's score, and he scored on that drive.
signals.quote: I'm like, all right, I want to get Brenton involved.

signals.claim: Tuten will keep a meaningful role in the run game, including more outside zone carries.
signals.note: Coen praised his yards after contact and his reads, and said he could have run more outside zone.
signals.quote: I thought he ran nasty. I thought he ran violent.

topics.detail: Coen wants the team playing grimy, physical and nasty in all three phases, and said the offensive line set the tone and the backs did well after contact.
The defense held Cleveland to three points after a short field following a long kickoff return, and added a big play late. Coen said kickoff coverage needs cleanup.
The staff practiced openers more on Friday and shared the opening script earlier in the week. Coen wants to carry that earlier preparation into normal game weeks.

title: Postgame Press Conference: John Harbaugh on first win as Giants' head coach
headline: Malik Nabers played after a pregame test and had a strong game; Jaxson Dart was excellent in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with Isaiah Likely a target on pinpoint throws.
summary: Harbaugh was proud of the team effort in the Week 1 Sunday night win over Dallas and called it a winning effort that was far from perfect. He praised the offense, especially Jaxson Dart, who handled a lot at the line and in the huddle and made some pinpoint throws. The offense went 9-for-10 on third down before the kneel-downs, and Harbaugh singled out the pass protection and said the offensive line, or possibly the D-line, may have been the position group of the game. Malik Nabers was cleared medically, but the decision to play came about 2.5 to 3 hours before kickoff, when he tested it himself and felt ready. It was his call, and he played a heck of a game. Jevon Holland's interception, which led to a touchdown, swung momentum along with an eight-minute opening drive of the second half, which Harbaugh called a 14-point turnaround. He was unhappy that a key player put the ball on the ground, but said he trusts that player. He admitted he is mad about a late drive that let Dallas get within eight, but liked the offense answering right away. He also spoke about the electric atmosphere, owner John Mara's presence in the locker room, and being grateful to be the Giants' coach.

injuries.detail: Cleared medically, tested it on the field about 2.5-3 hours before kickoff, felt ready and the decision was his; he played and had a great game.

signals.claim: Dart handled a heavy pre-snap and play-calling workload and will keep running the offense effectively as the starting QB.
signals.note: Coach praised his command, accuracy, and management of a complex operation, which supports his fantasy QB outlook.
signals.quote: It was it was a great performance by Jackson.

signals.claim: Nabers was medically cleared, passed his own pregame test and played a full, productive game.
signals.note: He is healthy enough to play and performed well, which eases injury concerns for fantasy managers.
signals.quote: Malik played a great game.

signals.claim: Likely was a featured target on accurate sideline throws from Dart.
signals.note: Harbaugh pointed to throws to Likely as highlights, suggesting a meaningful role in the passing game.
signals.quote: Some of those throws were just just pinpoint accurate type throws.

signals.note: His interception, which led to a touchdown, was a game-changing play and a boost for IDP value.
signals.quote: here comes Javon Holland out of nowhere like a lightning bolt

topics.detail: Harbaugh called the pass protection stellar and said the offensive line, or perhaps the defensive line, was the position group of the game. The offense converted 9 of 10 third downs before the kneel-downs.
He credited the offensive staff for creating difference-making calls, including the first touchdown run and the third-and-nine touchdown after a false start before halftime.

The Giants scored on a short field after the Holland interception and then took the opening second-half kickoff on an eight-minute touchdown drive. He wasn't pleased that a late Dallas drive got them within eight.
A player fumbled, which Harbaugh said he was not happy about, but the player and another teammate told him he can be trusted and Harbaugh said he trusts them.

Harbaugh described the stadium atmosphere as better than expected and said the team is on its way toward the vision but has a lot of work to do. He also thanked owner John Mara, who spoke to the team after the game.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference | Jets at Titans (9/13)
headline: Jets beat the Titans; Breece Hall ran for 102 yards and a TD, Kenyon Sadiq scored on the opening drive, and Omar Cooper Jr.'s ankle is a minor watch ahead of Green Bay.
summary: Glenn was pleased with the opening win but stressed there is a lot to clean up, especially penalties, the end of the first half and the late touchdown the defense allowed in a hurry-up situation. He praised the run game, noting Breece Hall's 102 yards and a TD and that Braelon Allen also ran hard before having a touchdown taken away. Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq scored on the opening drive, and Glenn said it doesn't matter who scores because the group is unselfish. He called quarterback efficiency a key to winning and said the QB (Geno Smith) did a good job but still has areas to improve. Glenn said the offense missed some explosive-play opportunities he wants to review on tape. On the defense, he credited a disciplined unit and defensive coordinator Duke for running the game plan while Glenn handled other duties. He disagreed with the check-down at the end of the first half, with no timeouts left and six seconds on the clock, but chose not to risk a Hail Mary interception. Two players are banged up: a groin (the caption says "Mika") and Cooper's ankle, and he isn't worried about either. Next up is Green Bay at home.

injuries.detail: Coach said "Mika" has a groin issue, likely Minkah Fitzpatrick based on the caption. Glenn will update during the week and isn't too worried.
Ankle injury (the coach said "coop"). Glenn will provide more information as the week goes on and said he isn't too worried.

signals.claim: Hall remains the lead back in a rushing attack the coach credits with winning up front.
signals.note: A 102-yard, 1-TD game shows Hall as the featured runner for a team that values the run game.
signals.quote: Bruce had like 100 and some yards, 102 yards and a touchdown.

signals.claim: Allen is a meaningful part of the backfield rotation alongside Hall.
signals.note: Glenn said Allen ran hard and lost a touchdown, which suggests a real role and possible TD upside.
signals.quote: I hate the fact that he got his touchdown taken away.

signals.claim: Sadiq is involved in the offense, including scoring on the opening drive.
signals.note: The rookie TE scored on the first drive, an early sign of a red-zone or scoring role.
signals.quote: It was just good to get him get him a touchdown

signals.claim: Smith is expected to keep playing efficient, mistake-free football as the starting QB.
signals.note: Glenn praised his efficiency and big-play throws while saying he still has areas to improve.
signals.quote: He's a damn good player. It's the reason why he's here.

signals.claim: Cooper has an ankle injury, and the team will assess him through the week.
signals.note: Check his practice participation before Green Bay.
signals.quote: I'm not too worried about them at all.

topics.detail: Glenn pointed to penalties, the end of the first half and the touchdown allowed in a hurry-up situation as things to fix.
Explosive plays are a stated key to winning. He felt the offense missed more opportunities than it hit and will study the tape. The defense allowed no explosives.
Glenn disagreed with the check-down with no timeouts left, wanting more yardage before clocking the ball. With six seconds left, he chose to end the half rather than risk a Hail Mary interception.
Glenn credited a disciplined, well-prepared defense and said coordinator Duke knows the scheme and ran the game plan while Glenn handled other duties.
Kicker Sanders did a pretty good job but had one miss, which will be discussed.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Falcons
headline: Steelers want a more balanced offense, with 25+ and closer to 30 rushes a week, and Darnell Washington should see more targets. Rodgers and the downfield shot plays look promising.
summary: McCarthy was pleased with the 20-13 home win over the Falcons, crediting a defense that set the tone with sacks and picks, including a signature T.J. Watt play that he called the biggest of the game. He called the offense "herky jerky," starting with himself, and said third-down conversions and penalties were the main problems. He also pointed to a special teams clock-reset communication breakdown. He said the downfield passing game has been the most productive he can remember this early in a season, and that the team came close to hitting shot plays against Atlanta. He did not like the gap between 18 runs and about 40 Aaron Rodgers pass attempts. He wants to be north of 25 rushes every week, closer to 30 plus, for complementary football. Asked about using Darnell Washington more, especially on third downs, he said the offense has plenty of opportunities for its perimeter players and he is confident Washington will get his chances. He said a cornerback referred to as Joey is finishing a ramp-up and is ready to do more, with snaps increasing Wednesday. He deflected questions about the contract side of that situation. He praised the defense as a whole and called one penalty on a corner's tackle a tough call.

injuries.player: Joey (CB, surname not given; not on provided roster)
injuries.detail: Active for the game but still finishing a ramp-up. McCarthy said he is "definitely ready to do more," will work tomorrow, and the team hopes to increase his snaps Wednesday. McCarthy declined to discuss the business or contract side.

signals.claim: Darnell Washington will get more opportunities in the offense as the season goes on, possibly including third downs.
signals.note: The coach says ball distribution is a planning priority, but he gave no specifics. Washington is a modest bump in TE targets, not a lock.
signals.quote: confident that Darnell will will get his get his opportunities

signals.claim: The offense will keep building its downfield throws and shot plays, which have been very productive in practice.
signals.note: Emphasis on deep shots helps the ceiling for Rodgers and the perimeter receivers, even though the offense looked uneven in Week 1.
signals.quote: as productive as I can remember of all the offenses I've been in

signals.note: Watt made the game's biggest play (a leaping catch that led to a defensive finish), a good sign for his IDP value.
signals.quote: great players make great plays all the time

topics.detail: The offense ran 18 times against roughly 40 Rodgers passes, which McCarthy said he does not want. He wants more than 25 rushes every week, closer to 30 plus, and attributed the gap to penalties and long down-and-distance situations. He did not name any running backs.
He called the offense a little "herky jerky," starting with himself, and singled out third-down conversions and penalties. He said the team came close on several downfield shots.
A communication breakdown around the clock reset cost the operation time, and McCarthy said the team can learn from it.
He praised the defense as a whole, including the outside corners with Joey not yet at full snaps, and called one penalty on a boundary tackle a tough call.

title: Todd Bowles on Season Opener: Limiting Turnovers | Press Conference
headline: Bucs lost Week 1 by a touchdown after four turnovers, three of them Baker Mayfield fumbles plus a Bucky Irving fumble; Jacob Parrish left with a back injury and is expected to get an MRI, while Benjamin Morrison and Josiah Trotter drew praise.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs lost by one touchdown largely because of four turnovers, which he said they can't afford, and he also pointed to penalties, false starts and missed tackles. He said the offense either turned it over or scored, and never punted. He described Baker Mayfield's fumbles as a mix: one or two came on scrambles, one in the pocket where he held the ball a bit, and one from behind that he never saw. The coaching point was to keep the ball high and tight. He denied that Bucky Irving's offseason shoulder surgery had anything to do with his fumble. Benjamin Morrison stepped in after Jacob Parrish went down and was praised for battling, being composed and covering well, though Bowles said he has things to learn. Josiah Trotter's pick-six got the Bucs back into the game, and Bowles called him a gamer who still has things to clean up. Parrish has a back injury and Bowles expects an MRI but had no further details. On the defense, he cited two missed chip-shot tackles on short passes that gained 8 or 9 yards, and said the two-yard slant touchdown came from a zone coverage breakdown, not a conflict between Parrish and Tykee Smith.

injuries.detail: Back injury during the game; Bowles said he's pretty sure Parrish will get an MRI but hadn't seen X-ray results.

signals.claim: Mayfield needs to protect the ball better after fumbling three times in Week 1.
signals.note: The turnover issues are a concern for his efficiency, but Bowles framed them as correctable ball-security fixes rather than a larger problem.

signals.claim: Irving's offseason shoulder surgery was not a factor in his fumble.
signals.note: Bowles dismissed any shoulder link, so there is no injury-related concern about his workload, though the fumble could be worth monitoring.
signals.quote: No, not at all. We just got to hold on to the ball.

signals.claim: Morrison stepped in at corner after Parrish's injury and will remain in a larger role if Parrish is out.
signals.note: Morrison could have a bigger defensive role while Parrish is hurt, which helps IDP and matchup considerations.
signals.quote: He was composed. I thought for the most part he covered. Well.

signals.claim: Trotter showed he can make plays in the run game and on the pick-six, so he will remain involved at linebacker.
signals.note: The pick-six and run-game plays boost his IDP value, though Bowles said he still has things to learn.
signals.quote: you can tell he's a gamer.

signals.claim: Parrish is expected to undergo an MRI on his back injury.
signals.note: His availability is uncertain, which affects the defensive backfield and opens more snaps for Morrison.
signals.quote: I'm pretty sure he's going to undergo an MRI.

topics.detail: Four turnovers, including a pick-six and one across midfield, were the main reason for the one-touchdown loss. Bowles said the offense either scored or turned it over and never punted.
Penalties and false starts hurt, and the defense missed chip-shot tackles on short passes that turned into 8-9 yard gains and extended drives.
On the two-yard slant touchdown, Bowles said there was no conflict between Parrish and Tykee Smith; it was zone coverage and someone should have been there.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Week 1 loss to the Jets: Titans offense managed one TD on nine drives, the QB missed throws he should make, and Jeffery Simmons' snap rotation is not changing.
summary: Saleh was frustrated but measured after the loss to the Jets, saying he expected a better performance and that New York was more physical in all three phases. The Jets leaned on the Titans in the run game, including a 19-play drive and a stretch of nine straight runs. They won time of possession by roughly 41 minutes to 18. Tennessee led 10-3 at halftime, but the second half fell apart after a poor punt, a failure to win field position, and a couple of explosive pass plays. The offense scored one touchdown on nine drives, and Saleh said the Jets' two-shell coverage shut down the run game, which only got going late. He said the quarterback missed throws he has to make and that the staff will keep working on it with him. He said the defensive line rotation will stay as is, with Jeffery Simmons held for third downs, two-minute situations and late in games, though he will review the tape. He called the team young, said the players are fine, and said they will grow through reps and film study. He also defended punting on fourth down from the 20 late in the third quarter, and said the challenge on the forced fumble failed by about a centimeter. On injuries, Jacob (likely Jacob Martin) was evaluated and needed an IV, and another player known as "DQ" was checked for a concussion. Both finished the game.

injuries.detail: Coach said a Jacob was evaluated and needed an IV but finished the game. The first name is the only identifier, so this is likely Martin.

signals.claim: Simmons' snaps will not increase; the defensive line rotation stays, with him saved for third downs, two-minute situations and late in games.
signals.note: His snap count should stay managed, which limits his volume even though Saleh calls him the best lineman, and the run defense was gashed when he was off the field.
signals.quote: I don't see the rotation changing.

signals.claim: Coaches will keep working with the QB on accuracy after he missed makeable throws.
signals.note: The Titans offense scored one touchdown on nine drives and Saleh acknowledged missed throws, which is a concern for passing-game production until accuracy improves.
signals.quote: he's got to make those throws. And he knows that.

topics.detail: Saleh said the Jets played a two-shell look and stopped the Titans' run game. A few second-half runs came too late to matter.
The Jets leaned on Tennessee for three to five yards a carry, including a 19-play drive and nine straight runs. Saleh said the defense must win its one-on-ones and that he must call it better.

Saleh defended punting on fourth down from the 20 at the end of the third quarter, saying the percentages were about the same either way. The team planned to manufacture a third possession and tried an onside kick later that failed.
The Titans challenged a possible forced fumble. The ruling was that the ball carrier's third point of contact was down by about a centimeter, and Saleh said the challenge was worth it.

Saleh said the team is fine and frustrated but not panicking, and he will watch the tape before making decisions. He called it a young team that will grow through reps, and acknowledged the boos from fans.
